title:
Give a fly
a memory
notes:
Set the context before opening the maze. The workshop asks how a fixed model can use external evidence in its next decision. We will implement a read path and a write path, then change whose observations are eligible. The fly is a concrete consumer that makes the effect visible.

The audience will choose a representation, bound a similarity query, constrain its candidate set, preserve evidence, and connect results to a decision rule. Those choices also appear in document retrieval, tool-result memory, and visual inspection. The workshop uses a scene-specific image descriptor and Qdrant Edge inside the Python process.

We will keep the neural weights fixed and compare eight independent flies under matched conditions. First, establish what the model controls. Then switch to the first demo. The slides teach the mechanism; the demos and builds show its behavior and implementation.

title: Change the input. Keep the wiring fixed.
notes:
Presenter cue: explain the input, fixed network, and readout boundary in two minutes. The neural details and feasibility results that follow are reference material.

The fixed network uses FlyWire v783: 138,639 neurons and 15,091,983 connections. A leaky integrate-and-fire neuron integrates current, leaks toward rest, and emits a spike at a threshold. The display uses real anatomical positions and computed spike IDs.

At each confirmed fork, the engineered sensor maps the two non-incoming visible options onto left and right LC10a visual-input cells. The more counterclockwise option maps left. Both channels receive 30 Hz for 200 ms. Forward movement pauses while neural yaw continues. The final calibrated descending-neuron rate difference selects the option by its sign. Six cells per side contribute to that readout. Zero repeats the window, up to five windows. Continued zero ends the attempt without an application tie-break.

A retrieved adverse observation suppresses the corresponding channel. The brain then receives different input, selects an opening, and controls its physical turn through the existing bearing adapter. The application engineers the option mapping, local sensing, and forward movement. Neural wiring stays fixed. This is an engineered interface around a connectome model. It does not establish biological planning.

The declared feasibility probe used 24 seeds and three initial sensory histories. Balanced input produced 50 left and 22 right choices. Suppressing either channel selected the other option in all 72 sessions. Report that left bias rather than tuning it away. Dense integration checks passed four cases, including persistent state. Brian2 scheduling equivalence remains unestablished.

Sources: fly_brain.py ; _internal/maze/neural.ts ; https://github.com/dtecx/doodle-fly/tree/2a8a0311e4e488e9bf9a7f8e79e42ffb8bcaadf5 ; https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-024-07763-9 . Hz describes input events per second in this model.

Point through the three steps once: the app supplies visual input, the fixed network produces spikes, and the measured motor readout controls selection and yaw. Memory will change the input at the first step. The image shows actual anatomical positions and computed navigation spikes; it is a static illustration, while the demo displays the current run.

The application supplies perception, option mapping, braking, and forward movement. The fixed neural readout selects fork options and controls every physical turn. The sensory rates are interface inputs, rather than vectors sent directly into biological neurons.

At 3:00, switch to the demo and run No memory. Keep all eight flies visible. Seeds 300-307 produce four exits in the opening group; A6 misses the 65-second deadline. Ask the audience to notice repeated traversal and chance successes. A single successful fly cannot establish a retrieval effect.

Return to slide 3 at 6:00. Do not explain query parameters during this first demonstration. No records from this stage enter the later Personal memory stage.

title: Retrieve evidence before choosing.
notes:
Define retrieval as selecting stored information relevant to the current input and making it available to the next decision. Vector search is the matching step inside this application. The consumer determines how the returned evidence affects the model input.

Follow the read path. The current entrance view becomes a query vector. Similarity search returns eligible records with their scores and payloads. The application chooses which evidence to apply and changes the sensory input. The fixed neural network then selects an opening and controls yaw.

Point to the external memory feeding the search. The write path adds a captured view and its completed traversal outcome after observation. Reading and writing are separate operations. A retrieved record is evidence about an earlier execution, rather than a direct movement command.

This workshop uses Qdrant Edge inside Python. The reusable pattern is observation, representation, constrained retrieval, and a consumer. The model can receive new external evidence while its parameters remain fixed.

Sources: _internal/maze/memory.py ; _internal/maze/simulation.py ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/overview/vector-search/ ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/edge/ .

title: The encoder defines what can match.
notes:
An encoder turns an input into a vector: a list of numbers used for comparison. Follow the picture through the encoder to the bars. The bars show 24 evenly sampled components of this actual query vector. Their vertical scale is enlarged for legibility. The complete vector has 192 values.

The fly uses a scene-specific descriptor. Its camera captures 64 by 64 RGB pixels from the current pose. Clear local compass rays orient the view toward an observed opening. A brightness and color-contrast mask removes the common floor and walls. Fixed channel constants [90,125,80] center the remaining landmark colors. Averaging each image column over depth produces 64 RGB values, then normalization gives a 192-value vector.

All constants are independent of traversal outcomes. The vector contains observed pixels only. It contains no coordinates, place IDs, hidden topology, or outcomes. Depth pooling tolerates movement along the corridor. Different approaches can still produce different views, and weak matches abstain.

This descriptor fits this simulated scene. For text, images, or tool observations in another application, choose and evaluate an encoder for that data. Query and stored vectors must use compatible representations.

Transition: similar views should produce similar vectors. Cosine compares their directions.

Sources: _internal/maze/vision.py ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/vectors/ .

Teach the representation as a design choice. Pooling over depth makes this descriptor less sensitive to movement along a corridor. It still depends on the visible landmark arrangement and camera protocol. The encoder determines which changes count as similarity and which distinctions can be lost.

For another workload, choose an encoder for its observations and evaluate matches using that workload's outcomes. A text embedding model, a visual model, and a structured event representation have different assumptions. Query and stored vectors must remain compatible, or the records need migration or separate eligibility rules.

title: Return a bounded set of candidates.
notes:
The read path returns a bounded candidate set. Explain cosine with the schematic rays and formula: compare vector direction after encoding. For unit-normalized vectors, cosine equals the dot product. Our descriptor normalizes its vectors.

The actual request uses Query.Nearest on the named view vector, limit 10, score_threshold 0.90, a payload filter, and with_payload=True. The limit is an upper bound, not a guarantee that 10 records return. A6's example returns one record, with cosine 0.9755296111106873, shown rounded to 0.976.

The threshold rejects weaker representation matches. The limit bounds the evidence available to the consumer. Higher limits can add repeated or conflicting records; stricter thresholds can discard useful evidence. Choose both using measured retrieval and consumer outcomes rather than treating the workshop values as defaults.

Cosine measures similarity under this descriptor. It does not estimate the probability that an earlier outcome will repeat. Payload provenance and the consumer's conflict rule remain necessary.

The rays are schematic. They are neither a projection of actual 192-dimensional data nor an HNSW traversal. If asked, HNSW provides a layered approximate-neighbor index; Qdrant supports filterable HNSW. This tiny shard establishes no production-scale performance result. Search time measures the local query call, excluding encoding and neural computation.

Sources: memory.py ; _internal/maze/vision.py ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/vectors/ ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/edge/edge-api/reading-data/ ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/indexing/ .

title: Rank within the eligible set.
notes:
Hold the appearance constant and change the record's metadata. Only the first row is compatible with this run. The second belongs to another maze. The third uses an older encoder. The repeated thumbnails and altered metadata are an eligibility illustration, not three returned observations.

A filter restricts which records can match. Our query requires the current world and protocol. World identifies the maze. Protocol identifies compatible encoding, camera, and controller assumptions. A high cosine score cannot make an incompatible record eligible.

Later, a source filter will select whose observations a fly can retrieve. In another workload, service, version, tenant, or access rules can set these boundaries. The application must enforce its access rules; these demonstration fields are not a complete authorization system.

Transition: the vector and the fields used by these filters travel in one Qdrant point.

Sources: pipeline.py ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/filtering/ .

Teach the logical candidate set, not a claim about the engine's physical execution order. The query asks for nearest neighbors among records satisfying world and protocol. Ranking globally and discarding incompatible results afterward can omit useful eligible records from a bounded result set.

The actual filter uses must conditions on world and protocol. In another application, tenant, access scope, service, or tool version may belong in the filter. A similarity score cannot grant eligibility. Enforce access rules in the application and query scope.

title: Store features with verifiable facts.
notes:
Point to the vector and payload as two different jobs. The vector represents the captured entrance view and lets us search by appearance. The payload tells us who observed the traversal and what happened. The outcome is not encoded into the vector.

A Qdrant point has an ID, vector, and payload. The example comes from A6's completed return to START. The payload includes source_fly, outcome, world, protocol, captured_at_ms, observed_at_ms, trial, camera_bearing, and the snapshot hash. Returned means a START crossing, rather than a terminal wall.

The application preserves the immutable captured image and verifies its content hash before display. The bars show 24 sampled components of the actual stored vector, with their vertical scale enlarged. Coordinates and evaluation route labels do not enter the vector or decision policy.

Transition: when can we write that outcome? Only after the traversal establishes it.

Sources: _internal/maze/simulation.py ; _internal/maze/presentation.py ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/points/ .

The visible payload excerpt uses A6's actual source, outcome, capture time, and completion time. The ID provides record identity. The vector provides the search key. The payload provides filterable attributes and the facts used by the consumer.

Keep facts needed for eligibility and interpretation in the payload. Preserve the evidence behind derived outcomes. A high-quality neighbor is still insufficient when its provenance, compatibility, or completion status is wrong.

title: Store completed observations.
notes:
Follow A6 through the three stages. It captures the entrance, completes a traversal, then stores the observation. The center drawing uses A6's measured path from its initial capture to the completed START return. It is a view of the recorded path for teaching, not a route supplied to the controller.

A6 captured this view at 4160 ms and completed the return at 19440 ms in the observation clock. The record becomes searchable after completion. The image and its hash stay attached to that outcome. A recalled guess never becomes a direct observation.

The detector uses returned for a START crossing, dead_end for a terminal wall, and open for another opening or the exit. Open records can expose a conflict; they do not certify a complete route to the exit. The consumer treats returned and dead_end as adverse evidence and abstains when the best conflicting outcomes have closely scored views. Agreeing duplicates do not cause an abstention.

Writes follow all current-cycle decisions. Later queries can use only completed observations. For an agent, store the observed tool result after execution completes.

Transition: we now have enough pieces to implement storage and retrieval in memory.py.

Source: _internal/maze/simulation.py .

Separate event time from publication time. captured_at_ms identifies the view at the start of a traversal. observed_at_ms identifies when its outcome becomes known. The vector keeps the captured view while the payload adds the completed outcome.

A pending traversal is not yet eligible evidence. Writes follow all current-cycle decisions, so another decision cannot use an outcome from its future. In an agent system, publish the observed tool result after execution completes. Choose freshness, update, and retention rules for that system.

title: Define the consumer policy.
notes:
The retrieval result needs an explicit consumer. Our supplied decide function keeps the best score for each outcome. It chooses the strongest adverse outcome among returned and dead_end. It uses open records to detect conflicting evidence.

If no adverse record exists, the consumer leaves the sensory input unchanged. If an open record exists and adverse_score minus open_score is below 0.02, it abstains. Otherwise, it applies the adverse record. The illustrated scores are teaching examples, not returned records from the demo.

In the first example, a 0.97 returned record has no conflicting open record. The corresponding left-option input can be suppressed, producing 0/30 Hz. In the second example, returned scores 0.97 and open scores 0.96. The 0.01 gap is below 0.02, so the consumer leaves 30/30 Hz and lets the brain explore.

The 0.02 margin is a tested rule for this toy descriptor. It is not a calibrated confidence estimate or a universal setting. Agreeing duplicate observations do not create a conflict. If both candidate options are excluded, the controller restores exploration rather than inventing an unobserved route.

Keep the stages separate: returned candidates, selected evidence, applied input, neural readout, and physical movement. Retrieval never directly supplies the turn. The fixed brain makes that selection from its changed input.

For another application, the consumer may add citations to context, propose a tool action, or abstain. Evaluate whether the evidence changes the desired outcome. Nearest-neighbor quality alone cannot establish that.

Sources: memory.py ; _internal/maze/memory.py ; _internal/maze/simulation.py ; fly_brain.py .

title: Build one: personal memory.
notes:
Switch to the editor. The slide is a map of the two functions; the editor shows their implementation. remember writes the supplied completed observation. recall searches for a view and returns eligible records with their payloads.

Open memory.py. Implement remember and recall. Keep the supplied decision function. Its result suppresses one sensory channel during neural branch selection. The neural readout selects the opening.

def remember(shard, point):
    """Add the supplied observation to Qdrant."""
    shard.update(UpdateOperation.upsert_points([point]))

def recall(shard, vector, scope):
    """Search the view vector. Apply the supplied eligibility filter."""
    return shard.query(QueryRequest(
        query=Query.Nearest(vector, using="view"),
        limit=10,
        score_threshold=MIN_SCORE,
        filter=scope,
        with_payload=True,
    ))

Run uv run run.py --check personal. Save and select Personal memory. Each personal run starts with an empty index. It receives no observations from the opening No memory demonstration. The fly must complete its own circuit before retrieval can change its next choice. The app reloads saved Python functions on each run. Sources: https://qdrant.tech/documentation/edge/edge-api/updating-data/ ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/edge/edge-api/reading-data/ .

The build implements the read and write mechanisms just explained. Keep the supplied decide function so the consumer stays fixed during this comparison. Store completed Points, return scored records with payloads, and preserve the supplied eligibility filter.

After saving, leave the slides and run Personal memory from 25:00 to 28:00. Each of the eight A flies starts empty and can retrieve only its own completed observations. No opening-demo records enter this stage. Six of the opening eight exit; failures remain visible.

Select A6 and inspect its first memory use. Compare the distinct query and stored captures, source, score, measured query time, and actual spikes. Its input changes from 30/30 Hz to 0/30 Hz. The gray path is the actual earlier matched no-memory run. Pause manually or use Replay memory.

Return to slide 11 for the shared-memory lesson. The demonstration has established what personal memory does. The next slides explain how ownership changes without changing the vector representation.

title: Ownership is a query constraint.
notes:
Memory ownership is a query constraint. Compare the eligible source sets before discussing a new implementation. A6's personal query selects only source A6. B6's shared query excludes source B6 and can retrieve the completed A group.

The query vector, named vector, cosine metric, limit, threshold, and decision consumer stay the same. World and protocol compatibility stay required. The changed source rule changes which existing observations may contribute evidence.

The cards show eligible sources, not ranked query results. Multiple records can exist for a source, and a source's eligible records may still fail the similarity threshold. Eligibility and relevance answer different questions.

Our B stage starts with an unchanged pool of completed A records. B observations are not published into it. This comparison avoids reading another B fly's future and keeps the evidence budget explicit.

In another system, separate ownership and access scope from embedding similarity. Personal and team memory can use the same retrieval mechanism with different eligibility rules. A filter is part of the application's access design, rather than a complete authorization system by itself.

Sources: pipeline.py ; _internal/maze/cohort.py ; https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/filtering/ .

title: Share completed experience.
notes:
Point to all eight A flies, the shared records, and all eight B newcomers. A6 is one source in the completed A group. Each B fly begins without firsthand observations and can query the completed A group before taking those routes itself.

The current comparison freezes that A pool. B observations remain visible as recorded evidence but are not published into searchable memory. The picture therefore has arrows from A to memory and from memory to B, with no B write arrow. It does not depict live cooperation or synchronization between devices.

Personal A flies could retrieve only their own observations. B newcomers can retrieve observations from any compatible A source. The matched seeds, maze, starting conditions, body parameters, and noise streams stay fixed across stages. The gray comparison replays the selected seed's actual earlier personal run.

Qdrant Edge runs inside this Python process. The same shard retains the original A records. The workshop demonstrates local filtered retrieval. Network synchronization is outside this lesson.

Transition: we will make that scope change in pipeline.py.

Make the publication protocol explicit. The A group publishes completed observations. New B flies read that pool. The one-way arrows reflect the workshop comparison; they do not imply that every shared-memory application must freeze its store.

A live cooperative system needs rules for when observations become visible, who may publish them, compatible representations, freshness, and conflicting reports. Network synchronization is outside this local workshop. Those design choices are separate from the similarity query.

title: Change the scope, keep the query.
Measure retrieval and behavior.
notes:
Return to the slides after the shared-memory demo. Separate retrieval verification from behavior measurement. Count failures alongside exits, then compare cost and errors under matched conditions.

The table shows a separate held-out evaluation, not the eight-fly opening group. Two groups of eight use seeds 50000-50015 with matched maze, initial poses, body parameters, and neural seeds. Each attempt has a 65-second deadline. Each mode uses the same declared neural seeds. Unfinished attempts remain in the mean time and failure counts.

Report these measures together:

Mode | Exit | Mean time | Mean path | START returns | Dead ends | Collisions | False exclusions
No memory | 5/16 | 56.1 s | 3177 world units | 28 | 9 | 0 | 0
Personal | 9/16 | 52.4 s | 2942 world units | 17 | 14 | 0 | 0
Shared | 16/16 | 19.3 s | 1122 world units | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0

Unfinished attempts count as 65 seconds in the mean. The longest non-deliberation stall was 0.0 seconds. Ownership, stored outcomes, retrieved places, and applied exclusions passed the audit. Declared seeds and failed controls remain in the evaluation records and archive.

These results describe one fixed engineered maze and a scene-specific descriptor. They establish neither general maze solving, biological planning, nor production search latency. Personal owners start empty. Shared B flies read the completed A pool. The source, world, and protocol filters constrain eligibility.

Transition: keep the same read, act, observe, and write pattern when replacing the fly with an agent.

Sources: _maintainer/evaluation-summary.md ; _maintainer/evaluation.json ; _maintainer/evaluation-protocol.json .

Separate retrieval verification from behavior measurement. Check source ownership, place compatibility, stored outcomes, conflicts, and false exclusions. Then measure exits, time, path, detours, and collisions. A fast query or high cosine score does not establish a useful decision.

Personal memory improves exits in this evaluation, while its mean time changes only modestly. Shared memory has completed experience from eight flies, so its evidence budget is larger. These comparisons establish a bounded mechanism in one engineered maze, rather than general navigation or biological planning.

title: Map retrieval to your own system.
notes:
Map the design choices, rather than giving a list of industries. For the fly, the query is a visible entrance. Memories are completed traversals. Compatibility uses world, protocol, and source. The consumer changes sensory rates. A completed outcome supplies the next record.

For an agent that reuses tool experience, the query can be its current tool observation. Records can preserve completed executions and their observed results. Eligibility may require tool version, owner, and access scope. Retrieved evidence can enter model context before selecting the next tool call.

Ask the audience to fill each column for one of their systems: what becomes the query, which records are eligible, and what the consumer changes. That defines a testable memory interface. Use an encoder suited to those observations; the fly's 192-value descriptor is not transferable to arbitrary text.

A document-answering system has a related read path and a different write policy. Verified documents and revisions enter its corpus. Generated answers do not automatically become facts. In a visual inspection system, comparable captures and observed inspection outcomes may supply the evidence. Choose compatibility, freshness, and conflict rules for each workload.

External evidence can change a fixed model's next decision without updating its parameters. The application still owns representation, eligibility, consumption, and evaluation. Measure the consumer's result and preserve the evidence that caused it.
